title: Playing with his brothers and his father's musical family
summary: He and Harold played together, Merrill accompanied him in church, and his father's family, including uncle James Bartlett Brown of a touring quartet, was very musical.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: To go back a bit to San Francisco, I believe you were telling me earlier that you and your brother had played together. Which brother was that?
Oh, the younger brother. The older brother was eight years older than I was, so we --
He was a piano -- concert piano type. And in fact he used to accompany me whenever I wanted to play a solo in church or something like that.
We played together quite a little bit.
And that was with which instrument.

I was trombone; by this time he had taken piano, and he was very good on piano. It seemed odd, but we were all very adept at understanding the styles and different feelings that we wanted to get out of our instruments. So we worked together quite well. In fact, later on we even played in the same orchestra.
I know you mentioned your mother played organ. Did your father play any instrument?

No, he used to -- he could play a little piano, and he was the singer. He came from a family of singers. He had one brother that was quite famous in a quartet that traveled all over the world back then, and his brother's name was James Bartlett Brown. I forget the name of the quartet. Oh, they were on the Orpheum circuit or Pantages circuit for years, and he traveled all over. In fact, the whole family was very musical.
